newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia intensifies search for oil.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia intensifies search for oil.

text.p: Indonesia has intensified its exploration for oil, especially in the eastern region, as it expects its reserves of nine billion barrels to deplete in 10 years, the official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.

Priyambono Muyosudirjo, director for exploration and production at state-owned oil company Pertamina, was quoted as saying on Monday that Pertamina had intensified its exploration, especially in the eastern region.
"With our reserves continuing to diminish and demand for fuel oil continuing to rise, Indonesia could sooner or later become a net oil importer," Muyosudirjo was quoted as saying.
He said the rise in demand was due to increasing economic growth which enabled more Indonesians to buy cars.
Pertamina president-director Faisal Abda-oe told Reuters last week that Indonesia needed two more oil refineries by 2000 to meet burgeoning domestic demand for fuel products.

He said the new refineries should each have a capacity of 125,000 barrels per day (bpd) to help meet demand in Indonesia, Asia's sole member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC). Indonesia has set its oil price at $16.50 per barrel in its 1997/98 (April-March) budget, unchanged from the current budget, unveiled by President Suharto on Monday.
